title: Qufu
summary:
This document is a comprehensive encyclopedia article about Qufu, a county-level city in southwestern Shandong province, China, best known as the hometown of Confucius. The article begins with an overview of the city's location, population, and its three most famous cultural sites—the Temple of Confucius, the Cemetery of Confucius, and the Kong Family Mansion—collectively known as San Kong, which have been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1994.

The document covers several major sections: the **Etymology** section explains the name's meaning ("crooked hill"), its historical English transcriptions, and its influence on the naming of Japan's Gifu city. The **History** section traces Qufu's past chronologically, from legendary times (Shennong and Shaohao), through its role as capital of the ancient State of Lu during the Spring and Autumn period, the imperial era under Tang, Song, Jin, and Ming dynasties (including the split of the Confucius family into northern and southern branches holding the Duke Yansheng title), to the modern era featuring the controversy over rerouting the Tianjin–Pukou Railway to protect the Confucius Cemetery's feng shui, and the PRC era detailing Cultural Revolution destruction of artifacts, the demolition and restoration of the city wall, and the city's modern administrative status.

Additional sections describe the **Administrative divisions** (4 subdistricts and 8 towns), **Geography** (city layout, rivers, and humid continental climate), and **Transportation** (rail lines including the Beijing–Shanghai high-speed railway, national highways, and an unfinished monorail project). A substantial portion details the **Sites related with Confucius**, including the Temple of Confucius (China's second largest historical building complex with its Dacheng Hall), the Cemetery of Confucius with tombs spanning over 2,000 years, the Kong Family Mansion, and a modern digital preservation project. The article concludes with sections on **Economy** (agriculture, industry, tourism, and mineral resources), **Education** (Qufu Normal University), **Religion** (Confucianism), followed by gallery, references, and external links.
